gap: No result ChatGPT got states any independently measured figure. Panbo's Ben Stein measured 202.4 Ah from a LiTime 12V 200Ah at a 10 A discharge and just under 110 Ah from an Epoch 12V 100Ah at a 5 A (20-hour) discharge. He also found that the basic LiTime 200Ah kept charging when its temperature probe was cooled well below 0°F.
standout_why: I opened the three pages ChatGPT cited. BatteryTrail's spec database says 'We did not test batteries ourselves for this page' and 'Every figure is a published manufacturer claim.' BoondockMaps says 'We have not lab-tested these units.' VanPowerCalc uses only maker datasheet figures plus general claims with no tester named. I also opened wildjoule.com (result 7), which says 'there is no test bay behind this site' and 'Specifications are manufacturer-stated.' None of these pages gives a measured capacity, a BMS thermal result or a cold-charge result from a named tester.
decides: This mostly confirms the pick rather than changing it. A named tester got at least the rated capacity from both brands: 202.4 Ah from a LiTime rated 200 Ah, and about 110 Ah from an Epoch rated 100 Ah. The cold-charge result is the useful part. Panbo found the basic LiTime 200Ah does not stop charging in sub-freezing cold. ChatGPT's advice to buy a model with low-temperature charge cutoff or self-heating is right, so RV owners who camp in winter should take the LiTime 230Ah with low-temp protection or the 200Ah Plus Self-Heating, not the basic 200Ah. Epoch's 120 A continuous BMS sustained about 160 A in Panbo's test without shutting down, which supports Epoch for owners running a large inverter. Two limits: the units Panbo tested are earlier versions (2023), not the exact models ChatGPT showed as cards, and I could not source a measurement of Battle Born.

findings.label: Measured capacity
findings.source_title: Li Time LiFePO4, no frills, serious value (Panbo, Ben Stein)
findings.note: Ben Stein's rundown at 10 A lasted just over 20 hours. The article was published March 10, 2023. Stein says capacity was the same after his heavy-discharge abuse testing. The article does not give the charger or the cutoff voltage. Pack is 8 × 100 Ah cells in a 4S2P layout. Article price was $629.00.

findings.label: Low-temperature charge cutoff test
findings.value: Did not stop charging with the probe cooled well below 0°F
findings.source_title: Li Time LiFePO4, no frills, serious value (Panbo, Ben Stein)
findings.note: Stein chilled the temperature probe while the battery was charging, and the BMS never disconnected. He notes LiTime makes no low-temperature shutdown claim for this model. High-temperature cutoff worked: the BMS disconnected at about 250°F at the sensor and reconnected below 200°F.

findings.label: BMS heat under load
findings.value: FETs held at 155–156°F at 95 A. At 175 A the BMS shut off after about 3 minutes
findings.source_title: Li Time LiFePO4, no frills, serious value (Panbo, Ben Stein)
findings.note: Shop was at about 75°F. At 75 A the hottest FET reached 132°F. With the case top off, the battery sustained 150 A. Rating is 100 A continuous and 200 A for 5 seconds.

findings.label: Measured capacity
findings.value: Just under 110 Ah new and 108 Ah after testing (rated 100 Ah, built from four 105 Ah cells)
findings.source_title: Epoch Batteries, elegant drop-in LiFePO4 (Panbo, Ben Stein)
findings.note: Both figures are 20-hour rundowns at 5 A. Published Feb 27, 2023, updated Feb 9, 2024. The largest cell voltage spread Stein saw was 0.015 V. The article does not measure heater power, heater run time or low-temperature charge cutoff.

findings.label: High-current discharge
findings.value: About 160 A continuous with no BMS shutdown. A load above 150 A emptied the battery in under 40 minutes
findings.source_title: Epoch Batteries, elegant drop-in LiFePO4 (Panbo, Ben Stein)
findings.note: Load was a 2,000 VA inverter plus a heat gun. Terminal voltage was 12.5 V under the 150+ A load. Rating is 120 A continuous and 200 A for 30 seconds. In a reader reply, Stein says the BMS stopped charging above 100 A of charge current.

findings.label: Measured capacity fade under cycling
findings.value: 104.69 Ah at cycle 1, 94.87 Ah at cycle 600 (5.13% below rated)
findings.source_title: Testing LiFePO4 cycle ratings, are they accurate? (Panbo, Ben Stein)
findings.note: Cycles were 90% depth of discharge, charged and discharged at 0.5C, charged to 14.2 V. Capacity was checked every 100 cycles with a 5 A (20-hour) discharge to 10.5 V. Stein's projection to 80% end of life was 2,343 cycles at cycle 600. Published Nov 13, 2025, updated Dec 2, 2025. This is useful context for the 4,000+ cycle claims that every rival repeats.
